Generalized Linear Model for Multiply-Imputed SCF Data

Source: R/scf_glm.R
scf_glm.Rd

Fits a generalized linear model (GLM) to multiply-imputed Survey of Consumer Finances (SCF) data. This function works with any GLM-compatible family (e.g., binomial(), gaussian(), poisson()). It applies the model to each implicate, combines results using Rubin’s Rules, and returns a pooled summary with z-statistics and p-values.

scf_glm(design, formula, family = binomial())

Arguments

design

A multiply-imputed svyimputationList object, typically created via scf_load().

formula

A regression formula (e.g., hborrff ~ networth + factor(edcl)).

family

A GLM family function. Defaults to binomial() for logistic regression, but can be any supported family (e.g., gaussian(), poisson()).

Value

A named list with:

pooled

A data.frame of pooled coefficient estimates, standard errors, z-values, and p-values.

models

A list of glm objects fit to each implicate.

MIcombine_obj

The original MIresult object returned by mitools::MIcombine().

Details

Use this function when your dependent variable is:

  • Binary (e.g., logistic regression for hborrff ~ networth)

  • Count or rate-based (e.g., Poisson regression)

  • Any outcome modeled via the GLM framework

Internally, this function:

  • Fits glm() models on each implicate's data

  • Combines estimates using mitools::MIcombine()

  • Computes z-scores and two-tailed p-values from the pooled estimates

See also

scf_logit(), scf_ols(), mitools::MIcombine(), glm()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Logistic regression: Who is likely to have borrowed money?
result <- scf_glm(scf2022, hborrff ~ networth + factor(edcl), family = binomial())

# View pooled results with z and p-values
result$pooled

# Inspect first implicate's model
summary(result$models[[1]])
} # }
